subject.title: Feature Request: Automated Session Memory Preservation & Synthesis

question: Should OpenClaw core own structured reset/startup memory synthesis and transcript-linking, or should core only expose lifecycle/plugin hooks while memory plugins or MCP packages own the policy?
rationale: The unresolved work crosses silent model calls, private transcript retention, startup prompt injection, plugin APIs, configuration defaults, and overlapping lifecycle issues, which requires maintainer product and security intent before implementation.

options.title: Define a bounded memory-continuity contract
options.body: Make synthesis opt-in and specify redaction, retention, timeout, dedupe, audit, startup context limits, and tests before adding or expanding core behavior.

options.title: Route synthesis outside core
options.body: Keep core lean by treating world-model MCP or memory plugins as the owner and only add missing generic lifecycle APIs if the plugin path cannot support the workflow.

options.title: Split into narrower canonical issues
options.body: Let #45608 own reset-time agentic flush and #15828 own trigger/summary coverage, leaving this issue as an umbrella only if maintainers want an umbrella tracker.

recommendation.title: Define a bounded memory-continuity contract
recommendation.body: Make synthesis opt-in and specify redaction, retention, timeout, dedupe, audit, startup context limits, and tests before adding or expanding core behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: The existing agentic memory flush and reset/new behavior are the closest current-main ownership signals for deciding whether synthesis belongs in core.
